articles.headline: Who are Sabah FK, Barcelona's Champions League opponents?
articles.description: Sabah, a club near the Iranian border that didn't exist a decade ago, with a coach who owes his career to a Lithuanian quiz show, are in this season Champions League. How did they make it?
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナのチャンピオンズリーグ対戦相手、サバFKとはどんなチームか？
articles.descriptionJa: 10年前には存在せず、イラン国境付近に拠点を置くクラブであり、リトアニアのクイズ番組のおかげでキャリアを築いた監督を擁するサバが、今シーズンのチャンピオンズリーグに出場する。彼らはどのようにしてここまで登り詰めたのか。
articles.body:
As ever, the league phase of this season's UEFA Champions League is packed full of the biggest clubs on the planet.

From two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain to last season's beaten finalists Arsenal, from record 15-time winners Real Madrid to their bitter LaLiga rivals Barcelona, the competition showcases the best of the best from across the continent.

But among the great and the good of European soccer are some less familiar names, and some that was completely new to almost all fans around the world when the draw for this season's league phase was made. Sabah FK, making their debut in the competition this season, fall into that category. The team from Azerbaijan drew European giants Arsenal, Barcelona, and Manchester United for their first voyage at this level.

- Why Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball could soon be replaced

- How world record for longest men's domestic unbeaten streak was broken

So, who are Sabah FK? How did they get the chance to go toe-to-toe with the biggest clubs in Europe. And what was their coach's unique route to European football's showpiece event? Here is what you need to know about them.

Editor's note: This article was first published on Aug. 27, 2026 and has been updated

The club didn't exist a decade ago

Sabah FK was founded only on Sept. 8, 2017, so the club's first match in the Champions League proper may well fall on its ninth birthday. The team nicknamed The Owls hail from Masazir, around 20 miles north-west of Azerbaijan's capital Baku, with the Iranian border less than 200 miles south down the coast of the Caspian Sea.

Last season was a monumental one, not just for Sabah FK but for Azerbaijani football as a whole. Sabah won their first Azerbaijan Premier League title, completing a double by lifting the Azerbaijan Cup, and in the process breaking Qarabağ's grip at the top.

Baku-based Qarabağ had won 11 of the previous 12 league titles and last season became the first Azerbaijani club to reach the group or league phase of the Champions League, eventually losing to Newcastle United in the knockout phase playoffs.

Fast-track to the elite

It has been a rapid rise for Sabah, but it all started in somewhat bizarre fashion.

They entered the league system in 2017-18 in the second tier, the Azerbaijan First League, and were promoted after one season despite the fact they finished fifth. The top four in the league -- Khazar Baku, Qaradağ Lökbatan, Shuvalan and MOIK Baku -- all failed to get the license needed to enter the top flight. Instead, the spot was given to Sabah, who never looked back.

The speed of Sabah's rise, plus tricky and expensive travel routes from Azerbaijan, has resulted in a modest away following at times for European games. When Sabah arrived in Romania to play the first leg of their Champions League playoff against Israeli clubs Hapoel Be'er Sheva (held at a neutral venue for security reasons), they were greeted at the team hotel by one solitary ultra.

articles.headline: Man United crisis: How did it start? Who is to blame? Is Pochettino the answer?
articles.description: Struggling Manchester United find themselves in a familiar place and fans are getting tired of the cycle repeating itself. But can Mauricio Pochettino find the answer, or do the issues run deeper?
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの危機：始まりはどこにあり、誰に責任があるのか？ポチェッティーノは解決策となるか？
articles.descriptionJa: 低迷するマンチェスター・ユナイテッドは、またしてもお馴染みの苦境に立たされており、ファンは繰り返されるサイクルに疲れ果てている。しかし、マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノは答えを見つけ出せるのか、それとも問題はより根深いのだろうか。
articles.body:
There was certainly a logic to Manchester United's decision to hire former USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino; the crisis got so deep that any option beyond a "safe pair of hands" gradually slipped out of the equation. Indeed, with the club second from bottom in the Premier League and facing the real threat of relegation, an experienced manager capable of restoring order and credibility was the only sensible appointment.

Of course, Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, following an early red card for young defender Leny Yoro, was a miserable start to Pochettino's tenure, but we learned practically nothing about what lies ahead for United under his leadership from that game.

What we did learn from his appointment, however, was that the club have decided once again to place themselves in the hands of a strong figurehead. There are echoes of Louis van Gaal and José Mourinho -- though not in tactical terms -- and the hiring does suggest that United expect Pochettino's authoritative personality to bring the club back on track, almost single-handedly.

For the decision-makers at Old Trafford it was the best option, as there is extraordinary pressure when a club of United's size hits a crisis. It's easy to suggest that United should simply copy the modus operandi of the southern "B-clubs" -- Brighton & Hove Albion, Brentford and AFC Bournemouth -- and, with their vastly greater resources, easily find their way back to the top of the Premier League. But that ignores what a buildup of pressure can do to decision making.

At United, every poor run becomes a judgement on the entire project; poor results breed impatience, which subsequently encourages short-term decisions that undermine any long-term strategy. But after more than a decade of attempts at restructuring -- some more half-hearted than others -- the storied club find themselves in a familiar place, despite spending €2.86 billion on new players since the Glazers' takeover in 2005, and fans are getting tired of the cycle repeating itself.

So how did we get here? Who is really to blame for this situation? And will Pochettino buck the trend?

Trying, and failing, to replace Sir Alex Ferguson

United's problems can, at least in part, be traced back to how they handled the retirement of the Premier League's most successful manager in 2013. Ferguson's authority stretched a lot wider than his job description as "manager" entailed; he had spent 26 years shaping the club as he wanted and working closely with chief executive David Gill, including through the Glazers' takeover.

While his successor, David Moyes, inherited the same powers, the former Everton boss lacked the experience, influence and relationships that made Ferguson's system work. Yet, In October 2013, Ed Woodward -- who replaced Gill -- told the United We Stand fanzine: "We don't have a director of football because we back the manager." He then added: "He [Moyes] has the same power that Alex did."

articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂とニュース：ユベントスがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドのブルーノ・フェルナンデスを視察
articles.descriptionJa: 今シーズン末に契約が切れるマンチェスター・ユナイテッドのキャプテン、ブルーノ・フェルナンデスがユベントスのターゲットとなっている。「Transfer Talk」が最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes ,who is out of contract at the end of the season, is a target for Juventus, while United and Barcelona want to sign United States winger Mathis Albert from Borussia Dortmund. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Juventus have expressed an interest in signing Manchester United attacking midfielder Bruno Fernandes as a free agent in the summer, according to Tuttosport. They will face competition from AC Milan, who will try to reunite the 32-year-old with coach Ruben Amorim.It is felt as though the summer isn't the time for Fernandes to move to MLS or Saudi Arabia. Fernandes addressed his future on Tuesday by saying: "For us to start winning games and then we can start speaking about a contract." Inter Milan's Hakan Çalhanoglu is another midfielder being looked at by the Bianconeri.

- Manchester United and Barcelona have stepped up their interest in Borussia Dortmund and USMNT winger Mathis Albert, TEAMtalk reports. The race to sign the 17-year-old is already gaining momentum, and he is keen to play more regularly than he currently is under Niko Kovac, having got just 38 minutes in the Bundesliga so far this season. Albert has previously turned down approaches from Manchester City, Barcelona and Bayern Munich, while Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal and Liverpool have also monitored him.

- Bayern Munich are considering moves for Liverpool pair Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz plus Manchester City winger Jérémy Doku as question marks hang over the futures of Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala, according to TEAMtalk. The Bavarians' long-running efforts to sign Ngumoha could be blocked as the Reds are close to finalising a new contract for the winger, their interest in Wirtz has never wavered and Doku's lack of Premier League starts could aid Bayern's chances. Olise is in the sights of Barcelona and Real Madrid while, according to Football Insider, Liverpool and Arsenal are long-term admirers of Musiala.

- AFC Bournemouth don't want to let Junior Kroupi leave in January and are demanding £100 million for the forward, according to talkSPORT. The 20-year-old is the subject of interest from Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, with the latter also looking at Manchester United's Marcus Rashford. Even so, the Cherries are determined to keep their France international until the summer at least, and Kroupi would favour a move to Paris Saint-Germain whenever he leaves the Vitality Stadium.

- The relationship between AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and Roc Nation chairman Jay-Z could help bring Real Madrid forward Endrick to San Siro, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports. Brazil international Endrick, who is represented by Roc Nation, has started just one match for Madrid so far this season as the 20-year-old is firmly behind Kylian Mbappé in the pecking order. articles.headline: Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'
articles.description: Jobe Bellingham teased his brother Jude Bellingham after the Real Madrid star's outrageous goal in the Champions League on Tuesday, before handing him advice about facing Arsenal.
articles.headlineJa: ジョブ・ベリンガム、ジュードのワンダーゴールを揶揄し「すねに当たっただけだ！」
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日のチャンピオンズリーグでレアル・マドリードのスターである兄ジュード・ベリンガムが衝撃的なゴールを決めた後、ジョブ・ベリンガムは兄をからかい、その後アーセナル戦に向けたアドバイスを送った。
articles.body:
Jobe Bellingham teased his brother Jude Bellingham after the Real Madrid star's outrageous goal in the Champions League on Tuesday, before handing him advice about facing Arsenal.

Madrid's Jude scored a volley with the outside of his boot from outside the penalty area as his side hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 at the Bernabeu.

Meanwhile, Jobe's Borussia Dortmund held Arsenal 1-1 at the Emirates as Maximilian Beier cancelled out Viktor Gyokeres' opener.

Jobe, watching his brother's brilliant goal for the first time, joked to CBS Sports: "It's come off his shin, hasn't it?"

He acknowledged: "That's a great goal."

Jude's Madrid will head to the Emirates on Dec. 9 to face Arsenal in the Champions League, and he has received some advice from his younger brother.

"All the best to him," Jobe told Amazon Prime. "It's obviously a top opponent, Arsenal. They're a big physical team. So, all the best to Jude."

Jobe Bellingham notes 'mismatch' as Dortmund held Arsenal

Jobe Bellingham thought he'd given Dortmund the lead against Arsenal but was denied by the offside flag.

"Gutted," he said. "I am a bit unlucky at the minute. I am playing a lot higher with more runs into the box so, at some point, it will come. It would have been nice if it was today, back in England. But, next time."

- Niko Kovac hails Jobe Bellingham's development after England call-up

- Bellingham credits Mourinho 'full stop' for stellar form after Madrid stunner

But he did play a key role as Dortmund recovered from the early set-back to draw level.

"One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against [Myles Lewis-Skelly]. So, if it was a long ball, I don't want to say it's a mismatch, but I am obviously bigger. You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or [Ezri Konsa] then it would be a bit more difficult. I thought there was an advantage in terms of height [against Lewis-Skelly] and I managed to win a few flick-ons which got us up the pitch."

Jobe Bellingham wanted 'good impression' after England call-up

Jobe received his first England call-up in Thomas Tuchel's most recent squad, alongside his older brother.

"It's brilliant because it's where I went to be, competing against the top players," he said. "That's why I signed for a club like Borussia Dortmund. You get all these experiences, you get the opportunity [to be called up by] England, which is obviously for me and my family the biggest honour."

Although Jobe was made to wait for his debut cap, he felt at home in his new surroundings, saying: "Yes, for sure. And that's credit to the staff and lads. The level of training is, as you would expect, really high. That was the thing I thought about most going into the camp, because obviously I hear Jude talking about it, because you want to make a good impression in training."

articles.headline: Steelers bench struggling QB Aaron Rodgers, to start Mason Rudolph
articles.description: Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy has benched starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- A day after coach Mike McCarthy unequivocally told reporters that "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback," the Pittsburgh Steelers will start longtime backup Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

Rodgers, the team announced in a post late Tuesday night on X, will be inactive.

The move to bench Rodgers, who turns 43 on Sunday, was a coach's decision, sources told ESPN. That means Rodgers, who previously announced this would be his last season after a 22-year career, might have played his final snap.

The move comes as the team searches for a spark on offense amid Rodgers' struggles during Pittsburgh's two-game losing streak.

Rodgers has completed just 60.9% of attempts this season, marking one of his worst campaigns since he became a full-time starter with Green Bay in 2008. He has been sacked 31 times this season, surpassing last season's total of 29, and leads the league with 257 yards lost in those sacks.

His 18.9% off-target percentage ranks 28th of 30 qualified passers this season, ahead of only Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (22.1%) and the New York Giants' Jameis Winston (24.8%).

In a 19-16 loss against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, Rodgers missed a wide-open Jaylen Warren on a play that could have turned into a 30-yard score.

"I feel like I had to throw it maybe harder than I usually do to the backs," Rodgers said Sunday, explaining that Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean's movement on the play affected his throw. "But yeah, that was a missed opportunity for sure."

Rodgers returned to the Steelers this season on a one-year deal worth up to $25 million after going 10-6 as Pittsburgh's starter in 2025. The four-time MVP was also instrumental in McCarthy's eventual hire in Pittsburgh, suggesting general manager Omar Khan take a look at his former Green Bay coach during the hiring process to replace Mike Tomlin.

On Monday, McCarthy pointed to the struggles of the entire offense when asked how he evaluated Rodgers' play in the team's losing streak.

"Just like anything, when you talk about the quarterback position, I think there's things offensively we need to do better and that always benefits and leads into quarterback play," McCarthy said. "So I just need him to just keep plowing away. We got a lot of work to do."

Rudolph, a 2018 third-round pick by the Steelers, is no stranger to taking over in difficult situations. In 2023, Rudolph went 3-0 in the final three regular-season games when he took over for Mitchell Trubisky and Kenny Pickett as the team searched for -- and found -- a spark. That experience, coupled with his tenure in the organization and rapport with teammates in the locker room, sources told ESPN, was critical in making the decision to start Rudolph on a short week against the Broncos.

articles.headline: Erling Haaland: When Man City don't win 'you start questioning everything'
articles.description: Erling Haaland has reacted to Manchester City's latest failure to win by "questioning everything."
articles.body:
Erling Haaland has reacted to Manchester City's latest failure to win by "questioning everything."

City required an 86th-minute equaliser from Rayan Cherki to draw 2-2 against Napoli on Tuesday at the Etihad in the Champions League.

Napoli had twice taken the lead, and City's failure to take three points means they have won just one of their past seven matches in all competitions.

"We tried to push at the end for a goal but we couldn't," Haaland told TNT Sports. "Not good enough and we let them in too easily.

"We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want.

"Football is easy and difficult. When you win it's easy and you know what to do. When you don't you start questioning everything.

"The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy.

"We have so much quality so it's about getting the quality out in every payer.

"We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best."

Cherki: 'I don't care about my goal' after Man City held by Napoli

Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund gave Napoli a 55th-minute lead, before teasing the home support about his allegiance to the red half of the city.

Ayyoub Bouaddi equalised before Noa Lang gave Napoli the lead again. But Cherki rescued a late point which leaves City sixth in the league phase of the Champions League after five matches.

"I don't care about my goal, I wanted to win the game," Cherki told TNT Sports.

- Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres

- Bellingham credits Mourinho 'full stop' for stellar form after Madrid stunner

- Guardiola 'embarrassed' to say no to Italy, national team my 'next step'

"We tried to put all we have inside the pitch. Sometimes the game is not like you want, and today is like the last game, the last two or three games. We need to work more and come back for a win, just that."

City manager Enzo Maresca said: "We pressed very aggressive, we recovered the ball most of the time. Off the ball I think the team was good, from my point of view.

"We created a lot of chances but it was difficult. We expected Napoli to play a waiting game in a low block.

"We conceded few chances, and the goals we conceded could have been avoided.

"There is a degree of regret we didn't win but when you can't win, don't lose. We take the point and go forward."

Press Association contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Bellingham credits Mourinho 'full stop' for stellar form after Madrid stunner
articles.description: Jude Bellingham praised José Mourinho for helping him reach career-best form after the midfielder scored a stunning goal in Real Madrid's 5-1 comeback win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ベリンガム、マドリードでの鮮烈なゴール後、好調の理由は「間違いなく」ムリーニョのおかげと語る
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日のPSVアイントホーフェン戦における5-1の大逆転勝利で鮮烈なゴールを決めたミッドフィルダーのジュード・ベリンガムは、キャリア最高のコンディションに導いてくれたジョゼ・ムリーニョを称賛した。
articles.body:
Jude Bellingham praised José Mourinho for helping him reach career-best form after the midfielder scored a stunning goal in Real Madrid's 5-1 comeback win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.

Madrid trailed 1-0 at halftime before Mourinho made a triple substitution -- including the introduction of Bellingham -- and the home side then dominated, with Kylian Mbappé netting a brace, and Vinícius Júnior scoring his first Champions League goal this season.

Madrid are now top of the league phase table with 15 points after winning all five UCL matches so far, with a visit to Arsenal in their next European game on Dec. 9.

"Mourinho. Full stop," Bellingham told journalists at the Bernabéu, when asked to explain his outstanding form, with four goals in his last five club games. "I'm enjoying my football a lot. I love the coach, his staff, and my teammates help me a lot.

"That's why I'm playing well, because I have a lot of help."

Bellingham was asked if his displays with England at the World Cup -- where he scored seven goals playing behind Harry Kane -- had been the catalyst for his renewed goal threat.

"I don't know if it's because I'm playing as a number 10, it's having freedom," Bellingham said. " Freedom to move, to drop deep, to help build up, and to play higher up to finish.

"I think Mourinho has given me a lot of confidence. That's why I'm playing well, because I'm happy."

Madrid have now beaten Inter Milan, Roma, RB Leipzig, AEK Athens and PSV in the Champions League this season, despite some inconsistent performances.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho told Movistar. "We made changes, and Jude is a different player. He gives us what we didn't have in the first [half].

"It was a mental 'click.' In the first half we didn't find our rhythm, we didn't press, we didn't win duels."

Mourinho refused to reveal if he'd been angry with his players in the dressing room at halftime.

"The dressing room is like Vegas," the coach said. "What happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas.

"We spoke. We're friends, and we spoke."

"Once again, the first half wasn't good," goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois said. "In modern football, if we don't all run and do what the manager asks of us, it's impossible, especially against a team that presses you man-to-man.

"With the clips [Mourinho] showed us on the screen at halftime, you could see we weren't doing things right. That changed our attitude."

Madrid, who are three points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona, next play Alaves at the Bernabeu on Nov. 28.

articles.headline: 'He's like f---ing Busquets!' - Jules Ahoka is making an unlikely Premier League rise
articles.description: Making his first Premier League start on Saturday, Sunderland's Jules Ahoka made playing at Villa Park look like a stroll in the park. The 20-year-old Congolese midfielder looked at home as he helped the Black Cats earn a valuable 0-0 draw.
articles.body:
Making his first Premier League start on Saturday, Sunderland's Jules Ahoka made playing at Villa Park look like a stroll in the park.

The 20-year-old Congolese midfielder looked at home as he helped the Black Cats earn a valuable 0-0 draw, having stepped in for the injured Granit Xhaka, playing the full 90 minutes, and building on his excellent showing in the 1-0 victory over Chelsea before the international break.

He made 10 interceptions and clearances combined -- more together than any other player on the pitch -- and made several progressive passes to suggest that he's more than a one-dimensional midfield destroyer.

Ahoka's performance was busy, proactive, without the youngster ever looking hurried or hassled. It was an impressive feat against an Aston Villa side who hadn't lost in their previous six Premier League games, and he'd cut a similarly unruffled figure against Chelsea, after replacing Xhaka in the fourth minute.

His teammate, Belgium international Thomas Meunier, couldn't hide how impressed he was with his young teammate's composed performance.

"Six months ago, he was playing in Belgium for Royal Antwerp," Meunier told journalists, "and now he's like f---ing Busquets," he continued, referencing the legendary Spain and Barcelona midfielder.

It was a playful comment, but hyperbolically generous one as well, with Meunier acknowledging some of Ahoka's subtle qualities which are appreciated by his teammates.

Like the FIFA World Cup-winning Spaniard, Ahoka looks particularly comfortable receiving the ball in a crowded midfield -- a dream for a defence finding themselves under pressure and looking for a favourable outball.

He also appears to have time in possession, to have mapped out his next move, and to execute each move with efficiency and calm. There isn't much glamour in remaining concentrated, tracking danger, and breaking up nascent Villa attacks, but for a young man, in the rarefied air of the Premier League, Ahoka looked completely at ease.

Against Chelsea, on November 8, he had been named Player of the Match. Only one player registered more tackles in the match than Ahoka, while he also contributed three clearances and one valuable interception after being called into action early on.

A video shared by Sunderland's official handle caught his teammates cheering as Ahoka was awarded the post-match prize before he addressed the group. It was a small, warm and authentic moment, with Ahoka being celebrated by those who acknowledged his class in stepping in and performing with such conviction against Xabi Alonso's side.

That was only the midfielder's second Prem appearance -- following a brief cameo against Bournemouth in mid-October -- and the towering Ahoka is already looking like a fine asset for Regis Le Bris's Black Cats.

articles.headline: Chuba Hubbard makes the difference again in another tight Panthers win
articles.description: Chuba Hubbard had a second straight week with two touchdowns in Week 11 of the NFL season, and crucially, both performances have been decisive in nail-biting Carolina Panthers wins.
articles.body:
Chuba Hubbard had a second straight week with two touchdowns in Week 11 of the NFL season, and crucially, both performances have been decisive in nail-biting Carolina Panthers wins.

The Panthers edged the Baltimore Ravens 35-33 to go 5-5 for the season. As it stands, they are fourth in the NFC and on course to host a wild card game.

Hubbard - who is of Nigerian descent through his father - takes our Africa Player of the Week honors, narrowly edging Week 10 winner Emmett Johnson, who plays for the Kansas City Chiefs and has ties to Liberia.

Africa Player of the Week: Chuba Hubbard (Carolina Panthers)

Hubbard was the star of another offense-heavy week for Africa's NFL players. The Panthers running back's two touchdowns took his tally for the season to 11 - joint-fifth in the entire NFL.

The Panthers trailed 12-0 until Mitchell Evans' touchdown late in the first quarter. A third of the way through the second, Hubbard ran round the outside of Malaki Starks and dived over acrobatically in the corner for an 18-yard touchdown to give the Panthers the lead.

The lead then changed hands back and forth, with the Ravens taking it again before a Tetairoa McMillan touchdown put the Panthers back in front and then Hubbard added the extra two points.

The Ravens clawed their way back in front to take a 26-22 lead into the half-time break, but the third quarter began with a Panthers drive spanning eight plays in just under four minutes before Hubbard finally went over for another touchdown.

From there, two Ryan Fitzgerald field goals were enough to see the Panthers over the line. Had it not been for Hubbard's efforts, it is doubtful that they could have pulled it off.

Africa Moment of the Week: Boye Mafe (Cincinnati Bengals)

Mafe was hugely unlucky to end up on the losing side 22-20 against the Washington Commanders, but the moment he notched his third sack in the first half of that game for the Bengals was enough to earn Moment of the Week.

A son of Nigerian immigrants, Mafe sacked Jayden Daniels once in the first quarter and twice in the second.

The last of those sacks saw him break through the defensive line and then power through Brandon Coleman's last-ditch attempt to stop him before he latched onto Daniels and hauled him down.

The 27-year-old defensive end became the first player in the league to record three sacks in the first half of a game since Myles Garrett last November for the Cleveland Browns. Garrett has since moved on to the LA Rams.

Honorable mentions

Nigerian linebacker Princely Umanmielen was instrumental on defense for the Panthers in their win over the Ravens, just as Hubbard was on offense. The 24-year-old picked up 1.5 sacks.

Emmett Johnson, a running back of Liberian descent, had another impressive showing for the Kansas City Chiefs with 143 total yards and one rushing touchdown in a 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Paulson Adebo - a cornerback of Beninese descent - made an impressive interception for the New York Giant

articles.headline: Cooper Flagg has 24 points and 12 assists as Mavericks beat Nuggets 120-101 in NBA Cup contest
articles.description: — Cooper Flagg scored 24 points and tied a career-high with 12 assists as the Dallas Mavericks beat the Denver Nuggets 120-101 on Tuesday night, moving into the driver's seat to win their NBA Cup group.
articles.body:
DENVER -- — Cooper Flagg scored 24 points and tied a career-high with 12 assists as the Dallas Mavericks beat the Denver Nuggets 120-101 on Tuesday night, moving into the driver's seat to win their NBA Cup group. 


              The Mavericks can clinch a spot in the knockout round as soon as Wednesday if Phoenix loses at Houston. The stakes were high entering this game with both Dallas and Denver 2-0 in West Group A play. The Nuggets have never advanced out of the group stage in the NBA Cup. They're still in the running for a wild card.


              Reserve P.J. Washington Jr. had 14 points after missing the last two games with an illness. The Mavericks dominated Denver in points in the paint, 68-38, and fast-break points, 35-7, in extending their winning streak to four games.


              It was the 11th 20-point double-double for Flagg, tying him with Dwight Howard for the second-most by a teen in NBA history. LeBron James leads the list with 18. Flagg doesn’t turn 20 until Dec. 21. 


              Nikola Jokic, the Western Conference player of the week, finished with 18 points, 11 rebounds and five assists. Jamal Murray added 20 as Denver's three-game win streak was halted.


              Trailing by 19 at halftime, the Nuggets whittled the deficit to 80-77 with 1:11 left in the third. The Mavericks quickly built it back up. 


              The Mavericks were cold out of gate on Denver's red NBA Cup-themed floor, going 0 for 6 before hitting three straight 3-pointers. From there, they took off. 


              Dallas ended the first half on a 15-0 run to take a 58-39 lead as the Nuggets walked off the court to a smattering of boos. 


              Up next
              Mavericks: At Phoenix on Friday to finish group play.


              Nuggets: At Utah on Friday to wrap up group play.

articles.headline: Longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford dies at age 101
articles.description: Martha Firestone Ford, who served as the primary owner of the Lions from 2014 to 2020, has died at the age of 101, the team announced Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Martha Firestone Ford, who served as the primary owner of the Detroit Lions from 2014 to 2020, has died at the age of 101, the team announced Tuesday night.

"Over more than six decades with the Detroit Lions, she was a loyal and constant fixture of the franchise, sharing in its history and traditions," the team said in a statement announcing her death. "She remained present with the team even this season, attending games with a devotion that endured throughout her life."

No cause of death was given, although the team said she died at home surrounded by her family.

Ford and her husband, William Clay Ford Sr., bought the Lions in 1963, and she took over his controlling interest in the team after his death in 2014.

Although she seldom spoke to reporters or commented publicly on the direction of the franchise, her influence was felt. She was in charge of the team from 2014 until 2020, when she turned the Lions over to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp.

Ford had since served as chair emeritus.

"Martha was special," NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "She cared so deeply about her family, the players, their fans, and the city of Detroit. She was committed to making the Lions -- and the game of football -- better. Martha and her husband, William Clay Ford, led the franchise with dignity and integrity. We will miss her kindness and sweet sense of humor. We extend our deepest condolences to her children, the entire Ford family, and the Lions' organization."

The Lions made the playoffs in Ford's first year in charge in 2014 but lost seven of their first eight games the following season. In November 2015, the team fired its president and general manager in a midseason shake-up. When Ford announced the changes, she told fans the franchise intended to "identify and hire the very best leadership in order to produce a consistently, winning football team."

The Lions played better down the stretch that season, and after hiring Bob Quinn as their new general manager, they returned to the playoffs a year later.

Although Ford kept a low profile, the 2015 shakeup was a sign that she was more than willing to bring about change in an effort to reverse the team's fortunes. Then-coach Jim Caldwell said she was very much a presence within the organization.

"I think visible ownership is great, and Mrs. Ford does it extremely well," Caldwell said in 2015. "She's there before games and she's there after games, and I think guys enjoy that part of it. She comes to practice and things of that nature, so it's been fun."

Ford also made an impact in the Detroit community. She was an officer on the board for Detroit Lions Charities and on the board of the Henry Ford Health System. Martha and William Clay Ford were credited with helping establish the Maplegrove Center, a substance abuse treatment facility in West Bloomfield, Michigan.

articles.descriptionJa: ワイドレシーバーのブランドン・アイユクは、水曜日にコマンダーズを訪問する予定であると、代理人のドリュー・ローゼンハウスがESPNのアダム・シェフターに語った。
articles.body:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Washington Commanders, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Tuesday, two weeks after the NFL reinstated him. He cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent.

Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024, and was placed on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list last December. He could not be removed from that list until he reported and passed a physical, which he did Nov. 9.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk told 49ers reporters earlier this month. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100%."

Aiyuk is expected to work out for the Commanders during Wednesday's visit.

In 2023, his last full season before his injury, Aiyuk was named second-team All-Pro after catching 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State during the 2019 season. However, a rift in their relationship appeared to have developed following a series of social media posts by the receiver. Aiyuk targeted Daniels in several posts and in one referenced Daniels' mother.

Daniels and Aiyuk spoke more than a month ago to clear the air, according to multiple sources.

Daniels befriended Aiyuk early in their time together at ASU -- before Daniels had won the starting quarterback job. During workouts, Daniels would throw with Aiyuk, who was going into his senior season and coming off a 33-catch, 474-yard season.

They quickly developed a rapport as Aiyuk ended the season with Associated Press All-America honors after catching 65 passes for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns.

ESPN's John Keim contributed to this report.
